question: Given the proven OOB READ (GHOST-SUBST-001, service_scan.cc:813), does a matching OOB WRITE exist in the same pipeline that could convert it to RCE?

method.harness: fuzz_matchpipeline — constructs real ServiceProbeMatch objects via InitMatch with genuine probe-file match lines ($1, $P, $SUBST multi-char, $I integer, CPE templates), then drives the FULL testMatch pipeline: PCRE2 match -> ovector -> getVersionStr -> dotmplsubst -> every substvar handler
method.design_detail: capture groups are followed by a 16-byte required suffix (TAILTAILTAILTAIL) so they end >= findstrlen-1 bytes before the buffer end — the KNOWN memcmp OOB READ is avoided, isolating the hunt to NEW bugs (writes)
method.refinement_discovered: the OOB READ condition is 'group ends within findstrlen-1 bytes of buffer end', NOT 'group at buffer end' — a 2-byte trailing ZZ was insufficient (fuzzer tripped the known READ on a no-ZZ input via $-before-newline matching); the shipped-probe analysis was re-verified against the refined criterion: all shipped SUBSTs have either 1-char findstr or groups bounded >= findstrlen-1 from the end

results.conclusion: No OOB WRITE exists in the version-detection template machinery. All writes are correctly bounded: dotmplsubst memcpy guarded by newstrend; strbuf_append grows via safe_realloc; Strncpy destinations match sizes; cstringSanityCheck copies bounded.

rce_conversion_assessment.write_primitive: NOT FOUND — machine-verified absent after 67.4M executions on the full pipeline
rce_conversion_assessment.leak_oracle_note: the memcmp result is a 1-bit oracle per position (subject bytes == findstr?), theoretically allowing adjacent-heap-byte probing — but the findstr comes from the LOCAL probe file, so a remote attacker cannot choose probe values; negligible remote leak potential
rce_conversion_assessment.verdict: GHOST-SUBST-001 is NOT convertible to RCE without a second, independent memory-corruption bug — and the 500M+ execution campaign found none in any reachable response-driven surface. The nmap 7.993SVN response path is write-clean.

campaign_totals.finding: GHOST-SUBST-001 heap-buffer-overflow READ at service_scan.cc:813 (unreachable via shipped probes; deterministic via custom probe; info-leak class)
